newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends higher on mill demand.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends higher on mill demand.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures closed higher on mill-buying and on firmness in the cash markets, traders said.

"We still have good mill demand in the spot markets. Here we are with one of the biggest crops in a long time and the premiums aren't breaking -- I think that's because the quality is so good that the mills are taking everything they can get," a MGE floor source said.
Traders also said wheat received support from a surge in CBOT soybeans tied to concerns over forecasts for cooler weather next week in the U.S. Midwest.
MGE spring wheat futurs closed one to five cents per bushel higher, with Sept up four cents at $4.56 a bushel. Dec gained 3-1/4 cents to close at $4.34 per bushel.
Traders said ADM, CIS and Atwood-Peavey each bought 600,000 Dec bushels. Wilson picked up 500,000 Dec bushels and Benson-Quinn sold 1.5 million Dec bushels, traders said.
MGE estimated Tuesday's spring wheat volume at 18.23 million bushels, versus Monday's volume of 16.487 million.
MGE barley closed steady to six cents per hundredweight (cwt) higher, with Sept unchanged at $7.40 per cwt. Dec gained six cents to close at $7.46 per cwt.
